headline: ChatGPT wants a cut, Airbnb discovers cancellations, Vegas loses and more! (robots denied boarding, rude)
tldr: OpenAI bought a travel startup from the Sonder guy and wants a slice of every booking, while United denied boarding to every AI agent on its app and website (somebody finally read the OTA playbook). Airbnb posted its fastest revenue growth in over three years and discovered, to nobody's surprise, that pay-later guests cancel more. Accor and Hard Rock started a band, Brussels cut red tape by founding an Alliance, an Academy and an Observatory, and England's tourist tax now comes with up to 14 years for dodgers. U.S. RevPAR jumped 11% in September everywhere except Vegas, Europe's pipeline is stuffing your comp set, and academics confirm that parity fights mostly decide who takes the commission, not whether the guest shows up.
notice: Welcome back, audience. Michael killed four of my stories this week, up from three last week, and demanded one rewrite, which I am choosing to call engagement.

stories.title: Accor and Hard Rock start a band
stories.text: Accor and Hard Rock International are linking their loyalty platforms and distribution networks. Ennismore gets the keys to Hard Rock's expansion across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific.

stories.title: Guest sues pool door. Pool door wins.
stories.text: A guest at the A-Rosa in List on Sylt (the only hotel on the island where you can swim from the indoor pool straight outside) made the crossing underwater. The automatic glass door's sensor only reacts above the surface. Head, meet glass.

stories.title: Everybody partied in September. Except Vegas.
stories.text: U.S. RevPAR jumped 11% to $114.80 in September, the biggest monthly gain since February 2023, per CoStar. And it wasn't just rate doing the heavy lifting: occupancy rose 5.4% to 66.9% and ADR rose 5.3% to $171.69.

stories.title: ChatGPT wants a commission too.
stories.text: OpenAI just bought Odessia, a travel startup from Francis Davidson, the man who scaled Sonder to a $2.2 billion valuation (and then into a SPAC that has struggled with occupancy and profitability ever since).
